configuration.connection_model: closed-loop persistent KV connections, one in-flight command per client
configuration.recovery_method: SIGKILL after the measured round, then fresh-process startup to PING
configuration.checkpoint_method: KV SAVE after recovery, measured client-side and via STATS checkpoint_pause_us
configuration.timing_method: STATS deltas measured with std::chrono::steady_clock; successes only

r4a_evidence.status: baseline instrumentation only; group commit is not implemented

timing_semantics.wal_append: write_all only; excludes encoding, rotation, and fsync
timing_semantics.wal_data_fsync: all successful WAL data fsyncs, including empty-segment creation
timing_semantics.sync_mutation: successful SYNC persistence path through in-memory apply; excludes network parsing/serialization
timing_semantics.max_fields: process-lifetime maxima at the end of a round; include preload/warm-up
timing_semantics.mean_fields: computed from measured-window counter and total-time deltas
timing_semantics.fsync_buckets: fixed 50 us through 100 ms upper bounds plus a greater-than-100 ms overflow bucket

limitations: WSL2 loopback, single node, same-host client and server; no bare-metal or production SLA claim.
Closed-loop clients with one outstanding command each; this is not open-loop saturation capacity.
The Python standard-library client competes for CPU and contributes to measured latency.
The 32-client configuration reaches the server's hard connection cap; it is not evidence for more than 32 clients.
SYNC includes one WAL data fsync per successful mutation on the owner event loop.
INTERVAL acknowledges after append and relies on a 100 ms timer or checkpoint/shutdown flush.
Recovery is measured at one quiescent crash point after each round, not across every possible crash point.
The compact artifact intentionally omits raw latency samples; per-round percentiles and variation are retained.
Timing counters are successful-operation cumulative values from steady_clock; they are diagnostic, not a production latency SLO.
Observed max timing fields are process-lifetime maxima including preload/warm-up; mean timing fields use measured-window deltas.
Fixed fsync buckets bound memory and cardinality but do not provide per-request traces or arbitrary quantiles.
This v2 artifact collects evidence for R4-A evaluation; it does not demonstrate that group commit is implemented or beneficial.
